sections.headline: A watchOS concept for YouTube.
sections.body: YouTube has no Apple Watch app. This is a concept for what one could look like, focused on the moments where the watch actually makes sense: a creator just posted, you want to queue it without picking up your phone, or you're playing something and want to skip.

items.label: My Role
items.value: UI Designer and UX Strategist, concept to prototype

items.label: Methods
items.value: HIG audit, constraint mapping, interaction design, micro-interaction spec

items.label: Tools
items.value: Figma, watchOS HIG, YouTube Design System

sections.label: The constraint
sections.headline: Platform Constraints
sections.body: A 41mm screen isn't a small phone. No keyboard, no swipe-heavy navigation, sessions that last a few seconds. I started with those constraints instead of trying to shrink phone patterns down.

items.text: Average glance duration on Apple Watch, the entire interaction had to work in one look
Existing YouTube app for Apple Watch, the gap this concept fills
Core use cases that justify a watch app: notifications, playback control, quick queue management
Screen height, every tap target minimum 44x44px per Apple HIG

sections.label: Design decisions
sections.headline: Design Principles
sections.body: Three rules before I designed anything. One action per glance, no hunting around. Scroll with the crown, not swipes, since swipes fight the watch's own system gestures. And haptic confirmation on anything you can't undo. I write rules like these before I open Figma on any project, not just this one. Constraints first, decoration never.

sections.title: Early wireframes, week 1
sections.sub: Produced in the first week after the HIG audit confirmed the three primary use cases. These focus on information hierarchy at watch scale: what goes above the fold when the session might last 6 seconds.

screens.label: Playback
screens.ann: This state had the most iteration. The scrub bar moved from top to bottom after several iterations. Bottom is more reachable when using the crown.

sections.label: Screens
sections.headline: Three states
sections.body: Three screens: playback with Digital Crown scrub, a browse and queue screen, and a full UI overview. Playback took the most rounds to get right. Scrub control at 41mm is harder than it sounds.

sections.before: Horizontal swipe navigation between videos. A natural phone pattern, but it conflicts with the watch's system-level swipe-to-dismiss.
sections.after: Digital Crown as the primary content axis: queue, scrub, and volume all on the crown. Swipes reserved for confirmations and back navigation only.

sections.body: The notification state is probably the strongest use case here. Two taps to queue a video without touching your phone. I kept it minimal to stay in scope, which was the wrong call.

sections.headline: Every screen stayed inside the HIG.
sections.body: Crown navigation throughout, haptic feedback on anything that matters, information density kept low enough to read in a glance.
